mappings.note: Instruction is to sort a list into combination, decomposition and displacement -- LO-1's classification clause word for word. The list itself is missing from the stored stem but the outcome is stated in the instruction.
Identifies the white precipitate from H2SO4 + BaCl2 as BaSO4, i.e. recognising a double displacement/precipitation from an observation. No equation is asked, so not C 1.3-LO-1.

Respiration as slow combustion 'to produce energy' is the standard exothermic-reaction item. Energy classification has no learning outcome in this frame, so competency level, consistent with qid:84798.
Picks the process that is NOT a chemical reaction -- physical versus chemical change, which no LO in this frame covers.
Names the law that balancing satisfies -- conservation of mass, which is LO-2 exactly, not the writing skill of LO-1.
Colour change on strongly heating FeSO4 is thermal decomposition read from an observation -- LO-1's decomposition clause.
Gas used to store fatty foods -- preventing rancidity, named in LO-2.
Thermite welding: identifying aluminium as the displacing metal in Fe2O3 + X. Displacement clause of LO-1.
Classifies neutralisation as a double displacement -- one of LO-1's six named types.
Names the reducing and oxidising agents in H2S + I2 -- redox identification under LO-1.
Turns on whether (s)/(l)/(g)/(aq) are correct at reaction temperature -- the physical-states clause of C 1.3-LO-1. Duplicate of qid:84831.

The stem supplies the classification ('is a decomposition reaction'), leaving only the 2:1 mole ratio to be read off the balanced equation, so the balanced-equation outcome and not LO-1. Duplicate of qid:84825.
A bare chemical formula, not an equation, so C 1.3-LO-1 does not apply; the competency 'represents chemical interactions and changes using symbols' is the right level for formula recall.
Completing 'Zinc + ... -> Zinc sulphate + ...' is equation construction, C 1.3-LO-1. Chose it over C 1.2-LO-1 because the blanks are reactant and product, not the reaction's name.
Formula of slaked lime -- symbol-level representation with no equation, so the competency rather than C 1.3-LO-1, same treatment as qid:104467.
Definition-to-name of a combination reaction, the first type listed in LO-1.
Use of slaked lime (whitewashing). A property/application recall with no reaction to classify and no equation to write, so competency level.

'Burning of natural gas is ... reaction' -- the expected fill is exothermic, an energy classification with no LO in this frame. Flagged as ambiguous because 'combustion/oxidation' would land on LO-1 instead, and the option text is not stored.
'Respiration is ... reaction' -- exothermic, the same energy-change gap as qid:104457 and qid:84798, mapped consistently to the competency.
Definition of quick lime (CaO). Substance identity, which sits under 'investigates the nature and properties of chemical substances'; no reaction is classified.
AgCl turning grey in sunlight is photolytic decomposition inferred from a colour observation -- LO-1, despite the stored 'Corrosion of silver and copper' tag, which is wrong.
Names the reaction class that produces a precipitate, i.e. the double displacement/precipitation clause of LO-1.
Loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen = reduced. The reduction clause of LO-1; stored concept tag 'Precipitation reaction' is wrong.

CaO + water named as a combination reaction -- LO-1. If the intended fill were 'exothermic' the item would belong at C 1.2 instead; the option text is not stored, so 'combination' is taken as the expected classification.
Blue vitriol = copper sulphate pentahydrate. A substance-identity recall item, so the competency rather than any reaction-specific LO.
Chemical formula of lead nitrate -- symbol representation without an equation, so the competency, matching qid:104467 and qid:104469.
'The reaction of water and quick lime is an example of' -- combination reaction, LO-1. Same reading as qid:104478 and mapped identically for consistency.
Number of water molecules in a copper sulphate crystal (water of crystallisation). A property of the substance, not a reaction, so the competency.
Selects the endothermic reaction -- the recurring energy-change gap in this frame, mapped at competency level.
Colour of FeSO4.7H2O. A physical property of a named substance; no reaction is being identified, so the competency.
A copper coin in copper sulphate gives no change, because a metal cannot displace itself. The item tests the displacement rule of LO-1 from its negative side.
Blue to green on dipping an iron nail in CuSO4 -- displacement identified from a colour observation, LO-1, not the corrosion outcome the stored tag suggests.
Names the gas from strongly heated FeSO4 -- identifying a thermal decomposition by its product, LO-1.
Brown NO2 from heating lead nitrate: thermal decomposition identified from the colour of the gas, LO-1.

Asks which observation shows that a chemical reaction has occurred AT ALL, which is a different skill from LO-1's 'identifies combination, decomposition, displacement... reactions'. No outcome in this frame covers reaction indicators, so the competency is the honest placement rather than a forced LO-1.
Evolution of a gas as evidence of a new substance -- a reaction-indicator item, same frame gap as qid:149842 and mapped to the same competency.
Classifies the observed bubbling as the 'evolution of a gas' indicator. The chemistry (Zn + H2SO4) is only the setting; the assessed skill is indicator classification, which has no LO here.
Why boiling bubbles are not a reliable indicator -- physical versus chemical change, doubly outside this frame's outcomes, so competency level.
Applies the indicator list to cooking egg white. Indicator recognition, not reaction-type classification, so C 1.2 and not LO-1.
Reaction-indicator recall. Mapped with the rest of the 149842-149856 indicator cluster to the competency, because the frame offers nothing finer.
Same indicator-recall skill as qid:149847 with different distractors; mapped to the same competency deliberately.
Explains a colour change as evidence that a new substance formed. Indicator reasoning, no LO available.
Warmth as an indicator, explained by bond changes. Both the indicator framing and the energy content fall outside every LO in this frame.

Rusting supplies the context but the question asks which INDICATOR is observed, not about corrosion's effects, so C 1.2-LO-2 would misdescribe it. Competency level with the rest of the indicator cluster.
Recall of the four observable indicators as a list. Purely indicator knowledge, which this frame has no outcome for.
One-mark recall of gas evolution as an indicator -- same cluster, same competency.
Assertion-reason on whether gas evolution always means a reaction. Indicator reasoning, no LO fits.
Assertion-reason on condensation and change of state as an indicator -- indicator plus physical/chemical change, both outside this frame's outcomes.
Which observation is a reliable indicator (vinegar and baking soda). Closes the indicator cluster; mapped to the competency for the same reason as the rest.
Best single piece of evidence that a reaction occurred -- reaction-indicator judgement, which has no learning outcome in this frame.
Why burning magnesium counts as a chemical reaction: a new substance is formed. This is chemical-change reasoning rather than LO-1 classification, even though the underlying reaction is an oxidation.
Which observation reliably shows a reaction with Zn and dilute H2SO4. Indicator selection, not displacement naming, so the competency.

Defines a word equation. C 1.3's competency text ('represents chemical interactions and changes using symbols and chemical equations') covers it, while C 1.3-LO-1 is specifically about a BALANCED equation with physical states, which a word equation has neither of.
Selects the correct word equation for magnesium burning. Word-equation level, so the competency rather than C 1.3-LO-1, consistent with qid:700184.
Convention question -- which side reactants occupy. Equation notation without balancing or states, so the competency.
Reads the reactants out of a given word equation. Interpreting equation notation, so the competency rather than C 1.3-LO-1.
Names 'products' as the new substances formed. Equation vocabulary, so C 1.3; the stored concept tag 'Combination reaction' is wrong and would have pulled this to LO-1 incorrectly.
